newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Three Chinese crude units to restart in May.
newsitem.headline: Three Chinese crude units to restart in May.

text.p: Three Chinese refineries are expected to restart their crude units in May following maintenance turnarounds, company sources said on Thursday.

Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co Ltd, which shut down its 100,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit in early April, is expected to resume operations in the first half of May, a source at the refinery said.
The southeastern 51,000-bpd Fujian refinery is also scheduled to resume operations in early May, a refinery source said.
"The maintenance work is still going on but we should be able to complete all the work in early May," the source said . The unit was shut down in the second half of April.
Maintenance works at the 100,000-bpd Dalian refinery are mostly completed and operations are expected to resume also in early May, a Dalian refinery source said.
"There are only some minor works left and most of the operations have started. We should resume full operations at the beginning of May," the official said.
The refinery, also known as the Dalian West Pacific Petrochemical Co (WEPEC), is jointly owned by several Chinese oil firms and French oil company Total.
